purpose: test whether the repeated Villavicencio network response is estimable after conventional opportunity and compatibility filters, without inferring decision-equivalence classes

traits_and_covariates.trait_subset: 45 plant species and 135 flower-visiting species with morphological data

primary_temporal_design.unit: adjacent subseason transition within a year

response_definition.primary_stage1_quantity: changed links among species independently present in both adjacent networks
response_definition.species_turnover_component: changed links for which at least one endpoint species is not present in both adjacent networks
response_definition.network_metric_claim: operational feasibility partition, not a new additive beta-diversity metric

presence_policy.preferred: independent species presence or abundance information
presence_policy.forbidden: silently equating zero observed degree with true absence

allowed_inputs: floral abundance or other opportunity covariates
compatibility_policy.forbidden: renaming trait clusters as decision-equivalence classes

decision_structure_policy.promotion_gate: only an independently measured cue-choice or decision layer may define decision-equivalence classes for Stage 2

stage1_success_gate: the 12 primary within-year transitions can be reconstructed reproducibly
shared-species opportunity is nonzero in enough primary transitions to estimate link change
species presence semantics are documented rather than inferred silently
trait and phenology covariates join without response-dependent filtering
a prespecified rewiring outcome retains estimable variation after conventional controls
stage1_failure_gate: the network and trait species identifiers cannot be crosswalked reproducibly
too few shared species remain after the trait-available subset is frozen
most apparent species turnover is inseparable from non-detection
no usable rewiring variation remains after conventional opportunity filters
claim_ceiling: Stage 1 can establish response feasibility only. It cannot validate environmental routeability or decision-structural turnover without an independent decision-structure layer.
